subject: eGFR

fixes.old: eGFR >60: standard (max 3600mg/day). eGFR 30–59: max ~1800mg/day. eGFR 15–29: max ~900mg/day. eGFR <15 / dialysis: specialist.
fixes.new: Gabapentin by creatinine clearance (SPC): ≥80 mL/min up to 3600mg/day; 50–79: up to 1800mg/day; 30–49: up to 900mg/day; 15–29: 150–600mg/day; <15: 150–300mg/day; dialysis: specialist.

fixes.old: Calculate dose reduction: gabapentin maximum 900mg/day at eGFR 30–59.
fixes.new: Calculate dose reduction: gabapentin maximum 1800mg/day at creatinine clearance 50–79 and 900mg/day at 30–49 (SPC).

note: The page contradicts itself: line 470 gives 1800 mg/day at eGFR 30–59 and 900 mg/day at 15–29, but line 93 gives 900 mg/day at 30–59. The SPC limits are 900 mg/day at CrCl 30–49 and 600 mg/day at 15–29, so line 470 allows up to twice the licensed dose. The pregabalin maxima (600/300/150/75) on the same page are correct.

subject: eGFR
correct: Duloxetine: no dose adjustment at CrCl 30–80 mL/min; contraindicated at CrCl <30 (SPC)

fixes.old: Renal function for duloxetine — contraindicated if eGFR <30; dose-reduce to 30mg if eGFR 30–60
fixes.new: Renal function for duloxetine — contraindicated if creatinine clearance <30 mL/min; no dose adjustment needed at 30–80 (SPC)

note: The SPC has no 30 mg renal dose reduction. The statement also contradicts cases/neuropathic-pain.html ('no dose adjustment needed for standard duloxetine').

subject: eGFR
correct: Mirabegron: 25 mg if CrCl 15–29 or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B); not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) or eGFR <15
source: https://www.geneesmiddeleninformatiebank.nl/smpc/h132822_smpc_en.pdf (mirabegron SPC 4.2; same as UK Betmiga SPC)

fixes.old: Mirabegron 50mg OD (25mg if eGFR <30 or severe hepatic impairment)
fixes.new: Mirabegron 50mg OD (25mg if eGFR 15–29 or moderate hepatic impairment; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment)

fixes.old: eGFR <30 or severe hepatic impairment: reduce to 25mg OD
fixes.new: eGFR 15–29 or moderate hepatic impairment: reduce to 25mg OD; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (SPC)

note: The SPC says severe hepatic impairment is 'not recommended', not '25 mg'. tools/clinic-guides/male-luts.html ('25 mg if eGFR 15–29') is already correct.

subject: eGFR
correct: Rosuvastatin is contraindicated at CrCl <30 mL/min (SPC). It cannot be continued at 20 mg.

fixes.old: If eGFR declines to <30: reduce to maximum 20mg.
fixes.new: If creatinine clearance falls below 30 mL/min: rosuvastatin is contraindicated — switch to atorvastatin (agree any dose increase with renal team, NG238).

note: This contradicts the same drug card ('eGFR <30: contraindicated') and cases/ckd.html.

subject: eGFR
correct: Dapagliflozin: not initiated if eGFR <15 (current SPC). Empagliflozin: not initiated if eGFR <20; dose 10 mg if eGFR <60.

fixes.old: dapagliflozin avoid if eGFR <25; empagliflozin reduce to 10mg if eGFR 30-45.
fixes.new: do not initiate dapagliflozin if eGFR <15 or empagliflozin if eGFR <20; empagliflozin dose is 10mg if eGFR <60 (SPC; glucose-lowering effect falls below eGFR 45).

subject: eGFR
correct: The SGLT2i SPCs set initiation limits (dapagliflozin <15, empagliflozin <20), and treatment is usually continued as eGFR declines, until dialysis. They give no stop rule at eGFR <20.

fixes.old: eGFR <20 → stop (insufficient benefit, AKI risk).
fixes.new: Do not stop for eGFR decline alone (expected early dip); initiation limits per SPC (dapagliflozin eGFR <15, empagliflozin <20); seek advice if eGFR <15 or on dialysis.

fixes.old: eGFR <20 → stop. Withhold on sick days
fixes.new: Do not stop for eGFR decline alone; seek advice if eGFR <15 or on dialysis. Withhold on sick days

note: 'eGFR <20 → stop' is not in either SPC. It contradicts the site's own advice to accept the eGFR dip (tools/clinic-guides/ckd.html: 'expect a small early eGFR dip — don't stop'). Owner may prefer to soften to 'seek advice' if a local rule exists.

subject: eGFR
correct: NICE NG203: do not modify ACEi/ARB if eGFR falls <25% or creatinine rises <30%; at ≥25% / ≥30% look for other causes, then stop or reduce. Stop if K⁺ ≥6.0.

fixes.old: Creatinine rise >25% or eGFR fall >25% → hold ACEi/ARB
fixes.new: Creatinine rise ≥30% or eGFR fall ≥25% → look for other causes (e.g. dehydration, NSAIDs), then reduce or stop ACEi/ARB

fixes.old: nephrology input if creatinine rises >25% or K⁺ >5.5
fixes.new: look for causes and seek advice if creatinine rises ≥30% (eGFR fall ≥25%) or K⁺ >5.5

fixes.old: Monitor: eGFR rise <25% acceptable
fixes.new: Monitor: eGFR fall <25% (creatinine rise <30%) acceptable

fixes.old: do not stop unless K⁺ >6 or eGFR falls >25% on initiation
fixes.new: do not stop unless K⁺ ≥6.0, or eGFR falls ≥25% with no other cause found

fixes.old: Do NOT stop ACEi/ARB unless K⁺ >6.0 or eGFR drop >25% on initiation
fixes.new: Do NOT stop ACEi/ARB unless K⁺ ≥6.0, or eGFR drop ≥25% with no other cause found

note: The site standard is 25% eGFR / 30% creatinine (tools/management/ckd.html, tools/prescribing.html, tools/management/hypertension.html). Two cases use a 25% creatinine threshold. One case says 'eGFR rise' where it means 'fall'. NSAID '>25% → stop' lines (chest-pain, axial-spa, low-back-pain) are a different drug context and were left alone.

subject: cabergoline
correct: Hyperprolactinaemia: start 0.5 mg per week (one dose or two 0.25 mg doses), increase by 0.5 mg/week at monthly intervals; usual 1 mg/week (SPC)

fixes.old: Cabergoline 0.5mg twice weekly (first-line)
fixes.new: Cabergoline 0.5mg a week, as one dose or two divided doses (first-line; SPC)

fixes.old: Cabergoline 0.5mg twice weekly (start; titrate up over weeks; endocrinology-guided)
fixes.new: Cabergoline 0.5mg a week (one dose or two; increase by 0.5mg/week at monthly intervals; usual 1mg/week; endocrinology-guided)

note: '0.5 mg twice weekly' (1 mg/week) is double the SPC starting dose. It disagrees with tools/algorithms/hyperprolactinaemia.html and the Clinic Guide. The same file also says 'twice-weekly dosing (compliance)', which is acceptable.

subject: urate
correct: NICE NG219: target serum urate below 360 µmol/L. CONSIDER below 300 µmol/L with tophi, chronic gouty arthritis or continued flares.

fixes.old: Tophi present → NICE NG219: ULT must be offered; target urate is 300 µmol/L (not 360 µmol/L).
fixes.new: Tophi present → NICE NG219: offer ULT; consider a lower target below 300 µmol/L (rather than below 360 µmol/L).

fixes.old: with a lower target urate (300 µmol/L to dissolve crystals)
fixes.new: with consideration of a lower target urate (below 300 µmol/L) to dissolve crystals

fixes.old: NICE NG219 target urate ≤300 µmol/L.
fixes.new: NICE NG219: consider target urate below 300 µmol/L.

note: cases/gout.html uses '≤360/≤300' (23 + 13 occurrences) where NG219 and every other page say 'below'. Replace all in that file only. Check after the first three edits, because they remove some ≤300s first. Also 'target urate 300 µmol/L;' in the tophi rows at lines 1139/1144: change to 'consider target <300 µmol/L;'. That string occurs twice, so replace it in both places.

subject: urate
correct: NICE NG219 offer ULT: multiple or troublesome flares, CKD stages 3–5, diuretic therapy, tophi, chronic gouty arthritis; discuss ULT with anyone after a flare. NG219 has no 'urate >600' or '≥2 attacks/year' criterion.

fixes.old: Recurrent gout (≥ 2 attacks/year), tophi, urate stones, CKD ≥ stage 3, urate > 600 µmol/L, or one severe flare.
fixes.new: Offer ULT (NICE NG219) for multiple or troublesome flares, CKD stages 3–5, diuretic therapy, tophi or chronic gouty arthritis; discuss ULT with anyone after a flare.

fixes.old: Recurrent gout (≥ 2 attacks/year), tophi, urate stones, CKD ≥ stage 3, urate > 600 µmol/L, or one severe flare.
fixes.new: Offer ULT (NICE NG219) for multiple or troublesome flares, CKD stages 3–5, diuretic therapy, tophi or chronic gouty arthritis; discuss ULT with anyone after a flare.

fixes.old: Initiate / titrate allopurinol if recurrent / tophi / urate stones / CKD / urate > 600.
fixes.new: Offer allopurinol (NG219) if multiple/troublesome flares, CKD 3–5, diuretics, tophi or chronic gouty arthritis.

note: These are outdated pre-NG219 (BSR/EULAR-era) indications in Ready Prescriptions.

subject: allopurinol
correct: Febuxostat comes as 80 mg and 120 mg in the UK; start 80 mg. There is limited data in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30), so get specialist advice.

fixes.old: Reduced allopurinol doses; febuxostat 40 mg OD with caution.
fixes.new: Reduced allopurinol doses; febuxostat 80 mg OD with caution (limited data if CrCl < 30).

note: 40 mg is a US strength and is not a UK SPC dose.

subject: urate
correct: If urate is low during a flare, repeat at least 2 weeks after the flare settles (NICE NG219)

fixes.old: Consider serum urate (may be normal acutely — recheck ≥4–6 weeks later)
fixes.new: Consider serum urate (may be normal acutely — recheck at least 2 weeks after the flare settles)

subject: bilirubin
correct: Jaundice usually becomes clinically detectable above about 40 µmol/L (sclerae first, in good natural light). Detection is unreliable near that level.

fixes.old: scleral icterus visible when bilirubin >35 µmol/L
fixes.new: scleral icterus usually visible when bilirubin is above about 40 µmol/L

fixes.old: scleral icterus visible when bilirubin >35 µmol/L
fixes.new: scleral icterus usually visible when bilirubin is above about 40 µmol/L

fixes.old: Clinically detectable jaundice requires bilirubin >50 μmol/L.
fixes.new: Jaundice usually becomes clinically detectable above about 40 μmol/L.

note: One page says 35 µmol/L and another says 50 µmol/L. Harmonise to about 40 µmol/L. Low clinical impact.

subject: bilirubin
correct: Gilbert's: mild unconjugated rise, occasionally up to about 80–85 µmol/L with illness/fasting; unconjugated >40 µmol/L → consider rarer causes (site Gilbert's page, BSG)

fixes.old: typically <100 µmol/L, with normal ALT/ALP/GGT
fixes.new: usually below about 40 µmol/L (occasionally up to about 80 µmol/L during illness or fasting), with normal ALT/ALP/GGT

fixes.old: typically <100 µmol/L, with nor
fixes.new: usually below about 40 µmol/L (occasionally up to about 80 µmol/L during illness or fasting), with nor

note: The article's 'typically <100' does not match tools/management/gilberts-syndrome.html, which says '>40 consider rarer causes; occasionally 80–85'. For the index file, the replacement assumes the index is regenerated. If it is, skip that fix.

subject: salbutamol
correct: BTS/SIGN 158: 2–10 puffs via spacer, titrated, repeated every 20–30 min (all ages). tools/algorithms/wheeze-child.html instead uses a fixed regimen for ≤5 years (4 puffs ×3 at 20–30 min, plus ipratropium) labelled 'local acute paediatric protocol'.
note: OWNER: under-5 acute salbutamol dosing differs across pages. wheeze-child.html gives 4 puffs repeated up to 3 times. cases/wheeze-children.html gives 2–10 puffs titrated. preschool-wheeze.html gives 10 puffs for severe. Keep the local fixed regimen labelled as local, or align it with BTS/SIGN 2–10 puffs (10 puffs for severe)?
